Looking at the error, the issue is that the code is generating year columns from 1991 to 2013 inclusive, but the actual dataframe only has specific year columns (1991, 1995, 1996, etc.), not all consecutive years. The error occurs when trying to access columns like '1992', '1993', '1994' which don't exist in the dataframe.

The fix is to use only the year columns that actually exist in the dataframe, excluding the 'Model' column.

~~~python
# Filter the row for Škoda Felicia
felicia_row = df[df['Model'] == 'Škoda Felicia']

# Get all columns except 'Model' - these are the actual year columns in the dataframe
year_columns = [col for col in df.columns if col != 'Model']

# Get the values for Škoda Felicia across years, ignoring non-numeric placeholders like '−' or empty strings
# Convert to numeric, coercing errors to NaN
felicia_values = pd.to_numeric(felicia_row[year_columns].iloc[0], errors='coerce')

# Find the year with the minimum non-NaN value
min_year = felicia_values.idxmin()

# The answer is the year as a string (or integer if needed, but preserve exact text)
answer = min_year
~~~
